hints: You need the actual paths, not just yes or no. What do you have to remember about the nodes above you while walking down?
Use DFS with backtracking: keep one shared path list. Add the node when you enter, remove it when you leave. At a leaf whose running sum equals target, save a copy of the path.

1. If the node is null, return.
  2. Add its value to path and to the running sum.
  3. If it is a leaf and the sum equals target, add a copy of path to the answer.
  4. Recurse into the left child, then the right child.
  5. Remove the last element of path before returning.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Build a brand new list for every node on the way down and check at the leaves.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One shared list with add/remove (backtracking); only matching paths are copied.
approaches.time: O(n·h) in the worst case (copying answers)

explain: In [2,3,1,null,1,4,0] with target 6, the root 2 has children 3 and 1; 3 has a right child 1, and the right 1 has children 4 and 0. Going left, the path becomes 2,3,1 at a leaf with sum 6, so we save a copy. Then we backtrack and visit leaves 4 (sum 7) and 0 (sum 3), which do not match, so the answer is [[2,3,1]]. Visiting left before right gives the left-to-right order the problem asks for. Always copy the path when saving it, otherwise later removals would change the saved answer.
recognize: "List every root-to-leaf path with a property" → DFS with a shared path list and backtracking.
